title: Scaling Multilingual Safety and Reasoning Evaluation through Reasoning-Guided Translation

body: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed across languages, yet their safety and reasoning capabilities remain predominantly evaluated in English. Translating existing benchmarks offers a scalable approach to multilingual evaluation, but preserving task-specific meaning across languages presents significant challenges, particularly for harmful requests, mathematical reasoning, and conversational interactions. We introduce a reasoning-guided translation framework for constructing multilingual evaluations designed to preserve the structure and intended meaning of diverse benchmark tasks. Our approach separates translation strategy selection from large-scale generation, combining reasoning-guided configuration selection with task-aware validation, targeted repair, and independent quality screening. Using this framework, we develop a source-aligned evaluation collection spanning seven safety, conversational, and mathematical reasoning resources across 11 languages. The resulting collection achieves 99.94% coverage of intended item--language pairs in the two subsets requiring repair. Evaluations of open-source LLMs reveal distinct language-dependent vulnerabilities, including inconsistent refusal behaviour and substantial reasoning degradation in lower-resource languages. These findings highlight the importance of task-sensitive benchmark construction and systematic quality assessment for understanding multilingual model behaviour beyond English.
summaryZh: 本文针对多语言大模型评估中存在的翻译质量问题，提出了一种“推理引导的翻译”框架。该方法通过结合推理配置选择、任务感知验证和针对性修复，确保了多语言基准测试在安全性、数学推理和对话任务中能够精准对齐源语言的语义与结构。研究覆盖了11种语言，揭示了开源模型在低资源语言下的推理退化和拒绝行为不一致等关键问题，为构建高质量多语言评估体系提供了系统性方法论。

确保翻译后的评估集与原始语言评估集在任务意图和难度上保持一致的评估方法。
针对特定任务类型（如数学、安全）进行的翻译质量校验。
训练数据较少、模型表现通常较差的语言。
模型在不同语言下对相同安全请求表现出不同的拒绝或接受倾向。
